title: An ordinary coefficient cone projects canonically after its derived-limit comparison
statement:
theorem diagonalTrace_exactConeComparison_projection
    {A : Type*} {B : Type*} {C : Type*}
    [Category A] [Category B] [Category C] [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [Abelian C]
    [HasLimitsOfShape ℕᵒᵖ B]
    [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasDerivedCategory (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ B)]
    [HasDerivedCategory C]
    (U : A ⥤ B) (V : C ⥤ (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ B)) [U.Additive] [V.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits U] [PreservesFiniteColimits U]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits V] [PreservesFiniteColimits V]
    (L : DiagonalRlim B) (M : A) (N : C)
    (π : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj (U.obj M) ⟶ V.obj N) (n : ℕ) :
    exactConeComparison U V L M N π ≫ (L.projection n).app _ ≫
        ((evaluation ℕᵒᵖ B).obj (op n)).mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((V.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app N) ≫
        (((evaluation ℕᵒᵖ B).obj (op n)).mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app _ =
      (U.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app M ≫
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor B 0).map (π.app (op n))

source.place: paragraph (1), Rlim of the system trace and its level-n reduction; expanded coefficient-cone normalization in steps 5--7

proof.text: Apply DiagonalRlim.normalization to the single complex of the tower H. Substitute the Q-factor formula for the evaluation/single comparison. Naturality and functoriality of Q reduce the equation to a cochain identity. At degree zero, limMap_π and the single-object comparison cancel; in all other degrees both maps are zero. This proves ordinaryRlim followed by projection and the evaluation/single comparison equals single(limit.π).

In an arbitrary category, naturality moves the inverse of a specified isomorphism across a natural transformation. Functoriality cancels its inverse against its forward map. Apply this identity to the exact-cone comparison, using the restriction/single isomorphism and the preceding normalized ordinary-limit projection.

The remaining single-functor composite is the image of limit.lift followed by limit.π. The ordinary cone lift equation identifies it with the given component π.app (op n). Precompose with the exact restriction/single comparison.
